summary: Re-review of tasks 4.13q and 4.13r (range c46161f..1572612, Red 82bf1c3/b021698, Green 427098d). Seven of the eight points hold in the code and each is pinned by a non-hollow failing-first test: the guard normalizes the NUL-separated cmdline and the fake daemon now spawns with a real argv split that writes its own entries at spawn (Option B), so D1/D2/D3/JD1 stop a real-split daemon and pin the raw entries; daemon_pids resolves HOME and cwd with realpath and compares on a path boundary, and D4/JD2 keep the `..`-HOME, symlink-cwd, and sibling decoys alive; daemon_pid_alive honors BENCH_OPENCODE_PROC and the N3 cases extract the production function verbatim against a fake table; the seed export falls back to /tmp when TMPDIR sits in a git work tree (S6/JS3/C11); the HOME guards refuse a relative job root and a resolved path outside the root (H1/H2); selection keys on integrationID with an ambiguous refusal and a provider-only entry never matches (C8/C9/C10 and the converted suites). My four gates rerun clean with the exact plan counts (65, 37, 22, 30) and no leftover process after any file. One blocking defect stays: point 8 is not wired in production. quota.ts runs ra-quota only when BENCH_RA_QUOTA is set (quota.ts:407-421); no file in this repo, in advantage-pr, or in heavy-run.sh sets that variable, and the code holds no default, so a live review-run of a Go route still reads through `openchamber status --json` -> GET /api/quota/opencode-go (quota.ts:422-429), the exact source the live probe-4.10 records as timing out. The plan row 4.13r claims `quota.ts --provider opencode-go runs ${BENCH_RA_QUOTA:-/home/daniebo/Desktop/advantage-pr/scripts/jobs/ra-quota} status --json` with 'else the default ra-quota path (production)' (plan.md:2397), and the Green handoff repeats the claim; the code contradicts both, Q16a-d pin only the seam with a fake double, and Q7 still pins the port source for opencode-go. Spec D15 still names the OpenChamber endpoint as the live Go source, so either the code needs the default the plan promises, or the plan and the PM order need reconciliation; the current phase record makes a claim the code does not meet.
blocking_findings: B1 Point 8 (the Go quota through ra-quota) is not wired on the production path. quota.ts reads ra-quota only inside `if (provider === GO_PROVIDER) { const raQuota = process.env.BENCH_RA_QUOTA ?? ''; if (raQuota !== '') {...return; } }` (quota.ts:407-421); when the variable is unset the flow falls through to `openchamber status --json` -> GET /api/quota/opencode-go (quota.ts:422-429). The runners invoke the tool with the ambient environment (review-run.sh:579, judge-run.sh read_quota), and `grep -rln BENCH_RA_QUOTA` over this repo, over /home/daniebo/Desktop/advantage-pr, and over heavy-run.sh finds only quota.ts, quota.test.ts, and the measure logs, so production never sets it. The plan row 4.13r states 'quota.ts --provider opencode-go runs ${BENCH_RA_QUOTA:-/home/daniebo/Desktop/advantage-pr/scripts/jobs/ra-quota} status --json ... Precedence: BENCH_RA_QUOTA, else an explicit --base/BENCH_QUOTA_BASE direct read (test seam), else the default ra-quota path (production)' (measure/tracks/model_guide/plan.md:2397), and the Green handoff repeats 'reads the Go quota through ${BENCH_RA_QUOTA:-.../ra-quota} status --json' (green-4.13r.log:13); the code holds no such default, so the third precedence case in the code is the port source, not ra-quota. Consequence: the live probe refusal of probe-4.10 line 4 ('opencode-go/mimo-v2.6-flash refused review-run: the quota state is stopped: quota: the quota read timed out') reproduces after the fix, because the production Go read still hits the endpoint that timed out. The Q16a-d cases pin the seam against a fake double and are real (fresh lastgood -> ready, 5h 96 -> wait, stale -> stopped naming stale, missing -> stopped naming missing), but no case runs the production shape (BENCH_RA_QUOTA unset, no base) against ra-quota, and Q7 pins the port source for opencode-go in exactly that shape, so the tests prove the seam and not the wiring. Fix direction per the plan row: default the command to ${BENCH_RA_QUOTA:-/home/daniebo/Desktop/advantage-pr/scripts/jobs/ra-quota} in the GO branch, with a Q17 case that runs the default path against a stub at that location or a relocated default; note that spec D15 (measure/tracks/model_guide/spec.md:734-746) still names the OpenChamber endpoint as the live Go source, so the PM must confirm the source switch while Green lands the default.
nonblocking_findings: N1 Point 3 (starttime before KILL) is implemented in both runners but pinned by no test, and the plan's no-test reason is stale after the same commit's N3 fix. The code is right: daemon_starttime strips to the post-comm fields and reads fields[19], which is field 22 (starttime) of /proc/<pid>/stat (review-run.sh:407-415, judge-run.sh:302-310), stop_daemons records it at TERM and skips the KILL on a mismatch or an empty recording (review-run.sh:481-486, judge-run.sh:376-381). The plan rules out a test with 'daemon_pid_alive reads the real /proc; BENCH_OPENCODE_PROC affects selection only' (plan.md:2392), but the delivered daemon_pid_alive and daemon_starttime both honor BENCH_OPENCODE_PROC, and the suite already signals processes it owns (D3's TERM-ignoring daemon receives TERM and KILL from the guard; killHelper runs in every finally block), so a deterministic case is constructible: a fake proc entry for a real TERM-ignoring decoy pid whose fake stat starttime the case rewrites between TERM and KILL. The guarded risk is low on this host (pid_max 4194304, a 5 s window), so this stays nonblocking.

N2 The Q16 assertion message 'the fake ra-quota never attempted the hanging API' contradicts its own expectation: `expect(api.requests, ...).toEqual(["/api/quota/opencode-go"])` proves the fake ra-quota attempted the hanging API exactly once with a short timeout and then fell back to the last-good file (quota.test.ts:1167-1169, 1188-1190, 1208-1210, 1226-1228). The expectation is right and the message is wrong; a future reader of a failure would look for 'no attempt' evidence that the case never collects. Message-only defect, no behavior gap.

Re-review dispositions of my c46161f findings: F1 resolved (withdrawn by fix, not contested): daemon_pids now joins the NUL-separated cmdline before the match (review-run.sh:447, judge-run.sh:342: readFileSync(...).split('\0').join(' ')), the fake spawns a real split via node -e with trailing args 'fake-opencode serve --service <tag>' (fake-opencode spawn_daemon_child), and D1/D2/D3/JD1 stop that daemon while the Option B pins read the raw entries the child wrote at spawn and assert at least 3 entries, serve and --service adjacent and separate, and no joined entry. N2 resolved: the HOME guards resolve real paths now - provider-credential.sh:52-77 refuses a relative or unresolvable job root and a call HOME that resolves outside it (H1 symlink, H2 relative folder fail at HEAD per red-4.13q.log:12), and the runners compare realpath '$JOB/home' against realpath '$JOB' on a path boundary (review-run.sh:697-708, judge-run.sh:481-492). N3 resolved: daemon_pid_alive reads ${BENCH_OPENCODE_PROC:-/proc} (review-run.sh:392-401, judge-run.sh:287-296) and the N3 cases extract the production function verbatim with shellFunc and run it against a fake table (running pid alive, zombie dead). N4 resolved: run_seed_export checks `git -C base rev-parse --show-toplevel`, falls back to /tmp, and returns 2 when /tmp also sits in a work tree (provider-credential.sh:182-192); S6, JS3, and C11 point TMPDIR into a fresh git repo and assert the recorded real-HOME export cwd sits outside it.

A5 (plan claims vs runs): plan rows 4.13q/4.13r claim 65 pass (65), 37 passed (37), 22 passed (22), 30 passed (30) - my four gates reproduce all four labeled counts exactly; red-4.13q.log:12 and :26 record the pre-fix failing states (review-run 56/9 with D1-D4, N3, S2-S4, S6; judge-run 33/4 with JD1, JD2, JS3, N3; credential-provider 6/16; quota 26/4) and green-4.13r.log:12 records the same pre-fix run plus the passing gates; no stale or false gate claim was found. The adversarial-p4-runner '14 passed (14)' claim rests on the Green log alone; it is outside this brief's gate list and was not rerun.

B1 proof (code): quota.ts:407-421 runs the GO branch only when `process.env.BENCH_RA_QUOTA ?? ''` is non-empty and returns inside the branch; quota.ts:422-429 then resolves the base from --base/BENCH_QUOTA_BASE and, when empty, from `openchamber status --json` and reads GET /api/quota/opencode-go; no default ra-quota path exists in the file (full read of quota.ts, 442 lines).

B1 proof (no setter): grep -rln BENCH_RA_QUOTA over this repo (excluding node_modules/.git/.opencode) -> harness/model-guide/quota.ts, harness/model-guide-tests/quota.test.ts, measure/tracks/model_guide/plan.md, measure/runs/model_guide/red-4.13q.log, green-4.13r.log; grep -rln over /home/daniebo/Desktop/advantage-pr -> nothing; grep -n 'BENCH_RA_QUOTA|ra-quota' over review-run.sh and judge-run.sh -> nothing; grep over heavy-run.sh -> nothing. The Q1-Q15 cases delete BENCH_RA_QUOTA in the sandbox (quota.test.ts:222) and Q7 pins the port source for opencode-go in that state, so the suite pins the seam and the port source, never the production ra-quota default.

B1 proof (live target): measure/runs/model_guide/probe-4.10.txt:4 records 'opencode-go/mimo-v2.6-flash refused review-run: the probe refused: the quota state is stopped: quota: the quota read timed out exit=2' at the pre-fix head, the refusal that point 8 answers; the production path after the fix is byte-identical to the pre-fix production path, so the refusal can recur. The real ra-quota does exist and its shapes match the new code: `ra-quota status --json` prints a top-level object keyed by plan id with 'windows' entries holding 'percent' (cmd_status, ra-quota:1672-1676), 'opencode-go' is a plan id of its config, and its own last-good fallback uses LASTGOOD_TTL_SECONDS = 6*3600 (ra-quota:231, lastgood_windows at :1369), so the promised default would work as written.

Point 3 code check: daemon_starttime strips `${stat##*) }` then reads fields[19]; with the full stat fields numbered 1 pid, 2 comm, 3 state, field 22 (starttime) lands at index 19 after the strip - review-run.sh:407-415 and judge-run.sh:302-310; stop_daemons records the value per pid at TERM and skips the KILL when it is empty or changed (review-run.sh:479-486, judge-run.sh:374-381); a failed starttime read at TERM fails open to the previous KILL behavior, an acceptable degradation.

Point 7 callers and coverage: SELECT_JS filters `entry.integrationID === provider && entry.active === true`, refuses two active entries as ambiguous, and a provider-only entry never matches (provider-credential.sh:152-155); the refusal names the ambiguity on both paths (provider-credential.sh:239-242, 258-262); the production callers of the helper are only review-run.sh:101 and judge-run.sh:82, and both suites now drive the real helper with live-shape store entries (storeEntry holds integrationID, no provider field), so the changed contract has no uncovered caller.

Quota callers and thresholds: the production callers of quota.ts are review-run.sh:579 and judge-run.sh (read_quota) and both leave the environment ambient; the test callers are quota.test.ts and adversarial-p4-runner.test.ts (base seam, unaffected by the GO branch). The new ra-quota path emits `stateOf(provider, answer.windows)`, the same function that applies the Go 95/100 thresholds on the direct path (quota.ts:385-394, 418), requires both a usable 5h and weekly window exactly like the direct GO path (quota.ts:412-416 vs 431-436), and leaves WAIT_PERCENT 70 and every non-Go source untouched, so the D15 thresholds did not change.

Option B (b021698) verified: the daemon child writes its own pid to the pidfile and its raw /proc/self/cmdline entries to '<pidfile>.argv.json' before its 120 s timer (fake-opencode spawn_daemon_child), and D1, D2, D3, JD1 read that file after the run (spawnArgvEntries), so the argv proof survives the stop of the daemon; git show --stat b021698 touches only the fake and the two runner test files, and git show --stat 427098d touches only the four production files, so the Green commit changed no test, as the plan row requires.
A3 check: every count in the plan rows and logs is a labeled integer from bun or vitest output ('65 pass', 'Tests 37 passed (37)'); no bare-digit count parse exists in the new cases.

A4 check: the new cases assert behavior, not presence: exit codes, one-line refusals (expectRefusal), the INFRA stderr line and infra record field, decoy survival by isAlive, the argv entries of the spawn file, the verbatim-extracted production helper, and the api.requests list of the hanging server; no 'deliverable present' check passes on a missing deliverable.

Process hygiene: no driver, no heavy-run.sh, no real opencode or openchamber command, and no signal to any process; all four gates ran one file at a time and each pgrep scan after them printed nothing of mine.

test_strategy_violations: B1: the point-8 ra-quota path is pinned only through the BENCH_RA_QUOTA seam against a fake double (Q16a-d); no case runs the production shape (BENCH_RA_QUOTA unset, no base) against ra-quota, and Q7 pins the port source for opencode-go in exactly that shape, so the plan row's production claim has no failing-first test and is false in the code.
live_contract_violations: B1: the live Go quota read of the runners (the probe-4.10 path) still goes through `openchamber status --json` -> GET /api/quota/opencode-go, the source the live probe records as timing out (probe-4.10.txt:4), because no invocation sets BENCH_RA_QUOTA and quota.ts holds no default.
prod_wiring_violations: B1: quota.ts:407-421 runs ra-quota only when BENCH_RA_QUOTA is set; review-run.sh:579 and judge-run.sh invoke the tool with the ambient environment and never set it, no file in this repo or in advantage-pr sets it, and the plan row's claimed default `${BENCH_RA_QUOTA:-/home/daniebo/Desktop/advantage-pr/scripts/jobs/ra-quota}` (plan.md:2397) has no counterpart in the code.

ratings.evidence: Seven of the eight points are right with edge cases covered (NUL join at review-run.sh:447, realpath scoping, git-free seed cwd, resolved HOME, proc seam, integrationID selection), but the production Go quota read still uses the port source (quota.ts:422-429) that probe-4.10:4 records as failing.

The Red record shows genuine failing-first cases (red-4.13q.log:12: 9/4/16/4 failures at HEAD) and the argv, N3, and Q16 pins are non-hollow, but point 3 has no test (N1) and the plan's production claim for point 8 has no test and is false (B1).
